text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak: We urge Israel to respond to peace committments. Israeli President Ezer "Weizman asked to visit us in fear of the situation," Mubarak told reporters while touring housing projects in new cities.
- A task force from four ministries to study how to invest excess water resources from the Nile in increasing farm land.

- "An agreement with the IMF on Friday will not include (new) burdens or price hikes," a cabinet source said. Al-Akhbar said it had learnt that the Paris Club of creditor governments would take a decision on Friday afternoon or Saturday morning to write off the third tranche of Egypt's debt, or about $4.2 billion, plus over $200 million in interest.
- Mubarak calls the youth to live in new cities.
- Economy Minister Nawal el-Tatawi said that the Egyptian government is exerting concentrated efforts to make the economic summit, to be held in Cairo in November, a success.
- Reports confirmed that Wednesday's earthquake did not affect archaeological sites or the High Dam in Aswan.
